pattern_id: Sync buffer double commit panic - already-committed block re-selected for synchronization
description: BUG PATTERN: Ordering node panic during synchronization due to attempting to commit already-committed block. DESCRIPTION: In a SmartBFT cluster with nodes being repeatedly stopped and started, an ordering node panics during the recovery/sync phase. The sync buffer fetches block 223 and commits it, but then the same block is selected again for synchronization (sequences 223-236). When the node attempts to submit block 223 a second time, it panics. ROOT CAUSE: The synchronization buffer's block range calculation does not properly exclude already-committed blocks. There's a race between the commit completion and the next sync range calculation, allowing committed blocks to be re-selected for fetching. LESSON: In distributed sync/recovery mechanisms: 1) Always check if a block is already committed BEFORE adding it to the sync queue; 2) Use proper synchronization between commit completion and sync range updates; 3) Implement idempotent commit operations that gracefully handle duplicates; 4) Test recovery scenarios with rapid stop/start cycles; 5) The window between 'committed' and 'sync queue updated' is a critical section that needs protection.
